lines.a0: So, you're the new Keeper. You don't look like a keeper, but then again, they never look how I expect.| Sit anywhere that isn't wet.
lines.a1: See that shelf? I set out a magic candle for every party member that goes down the Stair. I light it when you leave.| I pinch it out when you come home.
lines.a2: That's the deal. You come home, I pinch it out. Don't make me wait.
lines.a3: At the next table, a clatter of dice and a groan.
lines.a4: Let's play some dice! C'mon, papa needs a new pair of shoes!
lines.a5: That's Eren. He runs crates down the Doors for the Provisions Office. He has never once won at dice.
lines.a6: Statistically, Bet, that means I'm due for a win.| Hello! You're the Keeper. Could your heroes lend a man two silver? I gotta win one of these rounds!
lines.lend: Thanks chum!| ...And it's gone. Damn my luck!
lines.loaded: They're what?| ...Oh, that's why I keep losing! I knew I wasn't this unlucky. Joss! JOSS!
lines.b0: Say, are you going through the First Door? There's a cart of mine stuck on the rail cut past the gate. The wheel broke so I chained it up. The manifest's in the lockbox.
lines.b1: Count was off on the last run, too. Forty sacks of oil, a crate of hardtack, and six bags of rice.| Can't tell where the extra rice was lifted, but we felt the loss for sure.
lines.b2: Bring me that manifest and I owe you a drink. Bet, write that down.
lines.b3: You still owe me for the last team you sent down there!
lines.b4: That's why I'm not getting them the drinks till they return. Besides, this groups different, I can tell.

lines.a0: You've been busy, love. Sit. I'm Bet. This is the Low Lantern, the last warm tavern before the Stair.
lines.a1: You won't have heard, being down there. Workers have been going below on false papers. Someone's been circulating a false tithe called the Queen's Due. Rumor has it, it's a cult called the Dragon's Choir. One one hand they've been feeding half of Kiln Row. But on the other hand they've been pocketing the rest.
lines.a2: And every time you break one of those echoes, something in this Keep goes a little strange. Lamps go out. Wells dry up. And now frost on the inside of windows.
lines.a3: Eren can tell you the rest. He's been counting things again. Talk to the regulars. I have to tend to the candles.

lines.a0: Every lamp in my house went out. Same moment the Forge went cold, they tell me.
lines.a1: I went around and relit all of my magical lamps and cancled. I've poured drinks under this roof for eleven years. That's never happened before.

lines.a0: The First Door's quiet now, and my cart's still down there. The lockbox too. I'd go myself, but I've seen what lives down there, and I'm just not cut out for that life.
lines.a1: If you're ever back that way... please fetch the manifest. I need to see what we've lost and if I can get reimbursed for it.

lines.a0: You found it! I owe you a drink. I owe you two. Let's see what my wheel cost me...
lines.a1: Dragon claws.| Six of them. I've carried oil, hardtack, even a piano once, gods help me. I've never carried dragon claws.
lines.a2: "The Due has been received, V."| ...Right.
lines.who: A lot of names start with V.| A lot.
lines.mistake: I don't buy that, and I don't think you do either...
lines.knows: Veska. My boss. She signs everything V. She signed my birthday card V.| She's a complicated one, Keeper.
lines.c0: My mother lives in Kiln Row. If anybody knows what "the Due" is, it's her. She knows everything that happens on that street.
lines.c1: Hessa makes the stout. Go and see her. Take something sweet. She has a hell of a sweet tooth.

lines.a0: Eren. You were due at the loading dock an hour ago.
lines.a1: I was being thanked by heroes, Veska.
lines.a2: Then you were being thanked on the Office's time.| Hello Keeper, I am Veska, Provisions Registrar. Thank you for clearing the First Door. The camps below will be safer for my runners. That's no small thing.
lines.a4: A tithe arrangement for Kiln Row. Debt relief. It's registered with the Guild Hall and legal. Now Eren, it's eleven at night, I need you at the Dock. Now.

lines.a0: To the heroes of the First Door! A round of drinks for the whole room, Mistress Harrowgate.
lines.a1: Splendid work, really. Every door you open is a gift to us all. Keep up the good work.
lines.a2: Corvin's a generous man but I really can't stand him.| Something about him just rubs me the wrong way.

lines.a0: Kiln Row smells of hot iron and bread. Every doorway has a small clay lamp burning blue. Eren's mother takes the sweets, does not eat them, and likes you for it.
lines.a1: Every family on this street keeps a hearth-flame. It doesn't go out while the family lives. When someone dies, we let it go out.| We don't snuff it. We let it.
lines.a2: The Due. Six winters ago the Guild wouldn't give Kiln Row credit, and the snow came early, and we buried forty-one. The Choir came with grain.
lines.a3: Now we pay the Choir a tithe. And when a family can't pay, someone goes below for a season to work it off. Then they come home.| They used to come home.
lines.cult: It's a cult, love. It's also the only people who came. Both things are true on this street.
lines.who0: I keep a list. Nobody asked me to. Somebody ought to.
lines.who1: She gives you a folded sheet of names and seasons, tied with red thread. The last name is Tarn.
lines.who2: Tarn's my sister's boy. Eren's cousin. Went down last spring. His flame's still burning.| I check it every morning.

eren.trust.title: You ever wonder who's putting the bounties on the doors below, Keeper?

lines.a0: I've been at the Guild's records after hours. Don't tell Veska. Don't tell the Guild. Don't tell anybody, actually.
lines.a1: Every big bounty on the things at the bottom of the Doors is sponsored by the Aldane Expeditionary Trust. Corvin Aldane. You know the man.
lines.a2: And his Trust keeps its accounts at the same counting-house as V's Due.| The money comes from the same place for you to break those doors, as it does for my mother's neighbours to dig under them. That's the same counting-house.
lines.a3: Just seems strange to me is all, all those funds coming from the same place.
lines.a4: Barge people drink here too. One of them says there's a boat in the Third Door, low in the water. That boat is filled with boxes with strange stamps all over them.

lines.a0: Sit them down. Gently now.| There, there. What's their name?
lines.a1: You took a spear through the shoulder. It missed everything that matters. You're very lucky to be alive.
lines.a2: I'm Sereth. I'm here most nights, at the foot of the Stair. The Choir sends me supplies. I send them where they're needed.
lines.why: Because you're bleeding.| Is there usually another reason?
lines.what0: A family, mostly. Soup on cold nights. A doctor who'll come to Kiln Row. A song for the people to all get behind.
lines.what1: They call us a cult up here. I suppose we are. But we have hope, which is the part people don't like.
lines.what2: Every group needs a God. We had a mother once. The wardens put her to sleep and called it peace.
lines.what3: I don't want the world to burn, Keeper. I want her to open her eyes and see us. Is that so different from what you want from your gods?
lines.insight: (aside) He believes every word of it. And he's good at this. That shoulder will heal clean.
lines.religion: (aside) Five bells, one for each head. That's a devotional to Tiamat.
lines.end0: Come and find me before you go down. I'll have something ready for your heroes.| No charge. No hymn either, if you'd rather.

a2: "The Choir... I've heard of the Dragon's Choir before, what is it?"
what3: [Religion] Those five bells on his collar...

lines.a0: You're the ones from the grove. I'm Ilo. Bet says I can stay here till I recover. I've been here two days already.
lines.a1: We carry the Due. Coin, oil, rice. Down past where the Guild camps stop. Down to the big door, the one with no number.
lines.a2: There we stack it. Higher and higher every season.

lines.a0: I havent seen Dace in awhile. Last thing I remember he was saying the well-water tastes of ink. He's not wrong you know, it does taste strange.
lines.a1: See the corner? In the grey robes. They've recently started drinking here often. Quiet. Polite. But they stop talking whenever you walk past.
lines.a2: Half my regulars won't even come back now. They say the strange things happening prove she's desperate.| I just pour the drinks.

lines.a0: Sabeline at the Enchanter's had a look at that glass you brought up from the Drowned Star. Know what she said? "It's not a weapon, It's a tithe."
lines.a1: And Ilo says they are stockpiling it down there.
lines.a2: They're not digging down there, Keeper. They're carrying supplies. The Due goes to the Sixth Door. Somebody's building something under us, and they're paying you to clear the road.
lines.a3: I'm done asking people. I'm going to go and look.
lines.a5: I'll take Tuesday. Nobody is more trustworth than that mule.

lines.a0: Eren went alone except for Tuesday, his mule, down the Fourth Door last night. I told him it was wreckless, but he didn't listen.
lines.a1: Said if he wasn't back in a few days I should tell you.| Well, I'm telling you.
lines.a2: His candle's still lit, and it worries me, love.

lines.a0: Tuesday got home first. She walked the whole Stair by herself and stood outside Bet's door till somebody let her in.
lines.a1: They had me tied to a mirror, Keeper. They kept saying the Queen would want me whole. Like I was cargo.| I was to be a sacrifice Keeper!
lines.a2: Anyway. I owe you a drink. Hell, a round for everyone, on me!
lines.a3: Whatever you do next, I'm with you.
lines.a4: Noted. Now come get your drinks.

lines.a0: One candle on the shelf has been pinched out.
lines.a1: I kept his candle lit four days. I'd have kept it lit forty, but it went out on it's own.
lines.a2: Hessa came in. Asked me if I'd pinched it. I said no. She said her hearth-flame's still burning.| I think he may still be alive somewhere, only Ilmater knows in what condition.

lines.a0: Keeper. If this is about Eren's hours...
lines.a1: You put the names on the table.
lines.a2: ...Where did you get that.
lines.a3: Six winters ago the Guild refused Kiln Row any credit. Forty-one people died between the first snow and the thaw. I wrote every name down.| I'm a registrar after all, thats what I do.
lines.a4: The Choir came with hardtack and bags of rice. They only asked for our voices, and then for hands. A season's work below and the family's debt was forgiven. It was a good arrangement.| An offer I couldn't refuse.
lines.a5: What else do you want me to say?
lines.dates: I stopped writing them.| Not because I didn't know. Because I didn't want to keep writing a date and then crossing it out.
lines.letter: "Keep the Keep grateful."| That's Aldane's command. I've had a hundred different notes and guidance from them over the years.
lines.tarn: I know where Tarn is on the list. I know where everyone is on the list.
lines.m1: What do you want from me, Keeper?
lines.help: ...Then you'll need this.| Every name. Every season. Every date I didn't write on the official ledger. Keep it. I've kept it long enough.
lines.expose: Yes.| Yes, it does. Here. All of it.| But we can't leave out what our people went through. We picked the lesser of two evils, or so I thought.
lines.leave: By morning the Provisions Office is locked, and Veska is gone.

a5: "The last two seasons have no return dates."
m1: "The Keep deserves to know what you did."

lines.a0: Frost on the inside of the windows. The mirror behind the bar shows the room a heartbeat late. The argument has already started.
lines.a1: "DO NOT BREAK". No. It says don't do it! We have to tell the Keep. We have to stop the expeditions.
lines.a2: "DO NOT BREAK", huh. Eren would've had a lot to say about that mirror. Me, I'm not quite as sure.
lines.a3: You've read a cracked mirror and decided it's a curse, eh? I've read the hymn every day of my life. She's waking because it is her time, no other reason.
lines.a4: Stop the expeditions and the Choir stops paying, and Kiln Row starves again...
lines.a5: And what will you do, Keeper? Leave the last door shut, with four heads already loose and the last echo screaming?
lines.letter: "Keep the Keep grateful."| That's the Precentor's hand. He writes all our hymnals.| Why would he want you grateful?
lines.ledger: These are... I know these names. I tended him. And her.| Why are there no return dates?
lines.b0: The handwriting on the Trust slips. And on that letter. Same loops on the P. Corvin Aldane is the Precentor.
lines.b1: Aldane's coach left the Keep an hour ago. In a hurry. The bastard never settled his tab.
lines.b2: The Chronicler's still up. If you want the Keep warned, that's where you should go.

lines.a0: Every lamp in the Keep went out.| Every lamp. Every candle. The tower. The Guild. The Chronicler's little reading candles.
lines.a1: Even mine, but I was able to relight the single tavern light.
lines.a2: Several seasons ago I bought some magic oil, it's the only thing thats working.
lines.a3: Sit down, love. Everyone else has.

a4.scarred: They kept me in the dark a long time, Keeper. I don't mind the dark so much now.
a4.default: I'm handing out soup. Tuesday's carrying the blankets. Don't laugh, she's good at it.

lines.a5: I sit by his stool. His flame's out but I'm sure he's out there somewhere.
lines.a6: I've been reading names to people all night. Who went below. Who came back. They have a right to hear it from me. The candles no longer tell the truth.

a7.doubts: I cut the bells off. I didn't know what else to do with my hands.
a7.default: She's awake. Someone who loves her should be there when she opens her eyes.

lines.a8: Keeper. Where did the Precentor go?
lines.s0: Sereth kneels beside a wounded miner and goes back to work.
lines.s1: Sereth buttons his coat and goes down the Stair. He does not take a lantern.
lines.martyr: Then that's where I'm going. Someone has to ask him why.| Pour me nothing, Bet. I'll be back for it.
lines.stay: ...Yes. All right. Yes.| Hold this. I need both hands.
lines.r0: I copied it off the inside of the Sixth Door. It's open, by the way. You should know that.| I'll read it once. I don't think I can do it twice.
lines.r1: Hush now, Mother of Five. We give you five dreams to keep. To the Red, a forge that never cools, that she may rage asleep. To the Green, a garden of the dead, that she may grow and grieve.
lines.r2: To the Black, a drowning library, that she may hoard and never leave. To the White, a hall of mirrors, that she see no face but hers. To the Blue, a sky of falling stars, that she chase what never stirs.
lines.r3: Light a lamp for every dream, and let the lamps burn low. Break no dream that she is dreaming. Let no lantern-bearer go behind the doors to end them.
lines.r4: But should the dreaming fail, raise a champion at the height of power, for nothing less avails.
lines.r5: "Break no dream that she is dreaming."| No. Not now.| No.
lines.r6: ...Right.| Who's hungry? I got some rice and fish, and lots of beer.
lines.r7: This is a muster hall now. Everyone who wants to help, tell me. I was a quartermaster once. I can be one again.

a8: "Stay. They need a healer here more than he needs you."

lines.a0: I won't leave without the flames. None of us will. You understand?
lines.a1: You carry them up the Stair in clay pots, forty-odd small blue fires, one for every family on Kiln Row. Nobody drops one.
lines.a2: There. We can sleep anywhere now.

lines.a0: I'll read the names. All of them. Then you tell them what you found.
lines.a1: I tended half of them. They'll listen to me. I'll tell them what I believed, and then what I found.

a2.some: The Low Lantern is full to the walls. You read them {evidence}. Nobody speaks for a long time.
a2.none: The Low Lantern is full to the walls. You read them everything you know. Nobody speaks for a long time.

lines.a3: We paid her due. We paid it in coin and in children.| We're done paying.

lines.a0: I posted every Aldane bounty myself. I read the names on the Wall every morning, and then I posted his bounties.
lines.a1: They're down. All of them. And I'll stand on the Guild steps and say why, to anyone who asks and most who don't.
lines.a2: The Guild owes Kiln Row a winter. We'll start paying it now.

lines.a0: The tower lanterns were lit from her dreams. That's done. So we'll light them from mine.
lines.a1: One by one, every household in the Keep carries a flame from the Low Lantern's door up the hill. Kiln Row's blue flames go with them. By midnight the tower is burning ordinary oil.
lines.a2: There. Now it's ours.

lines.a0: There you are.
lines.a1: She sets a glass on the bar. The Last Light. On the house.
lines.a2: On the house.| Don't get used to it.

a3.fallen: {names}.| (She pours a glass for each, and sets them on the candle shelf.)
a3.none: (She looks at the candle shelf for a long moment. Every candle is pinched out. Every one of them came home.)

a4.scarred: So there I was, tied to a mirror, and Tuesday just walks in —| Fine. Fine, it was a different story last time. It gets better every time.
a4.default: So there I was, and Tuesday just walks in —| Bet. Bet, I'm telling it.

a5.captured: His flame went out last night. I let it.| Pour him one, Bet.
a5.default: Pour one for the ones who stacked her gold, Bet.

lines.a6: I'm doing the Keep's books now. Someone has to. I write the return dates in ink.

a7.martyr: Five small brass bells hang over the bar now.
a7.faith: A folded healer's apron lies on the end of the bar. Sereth did not come back.
a7.broken: Sereth is in the corner with a miner's arm in a sling, talking him through it.
a7.default: The corner where the grey robes used to sit is empty.

a8.captive: Somewhere in the Keep's cells, Corvin Aldane is writing letters nobody will send.
a8.default: A letter came for you this morning. Unsigned. It says only: "Splendidly done."

lines.a9: You said. Before any of us. I remember you said.
lines.v0: A letter from the Keep's cells, in a registrar's careful hand: every name on her ledger, and beside each one, at last, a date.

a0.slain: Quiet down there now, they tell me. Ordinary monsters. I'll take ordinary.
a0.stage5: Every bed's full and every pot's on. Go and kill her, love. I'll keep the soup warm.
a0.idle0: One candle per party. Yours is lit while you're below. Don't make me wait.
a0.idle1: I don't do prophecy. I do last orders.
a0.idle2: The Kiln-Row Stout's Hessa's. Don't tell her I said it's good. She knows.
a0.idle3: You look like you need a drink or a bath. I sell one of those.
a0.idle4: Frost, ink, hot hearths. Every time you come back up, something in this town is wrong. I'm just saying.

a0.slain: I'm buying a boat. I've never seen the sea. Tuesday hasn't either. We'll be terrible at it together.
a0.stage3: I count everything twice now. Crates. Stairs. People. Especially people.
a0.idle0: I lost again. But I lost less. That's a trend.
a0.idle1: Tuesday's a mule. Bought her on a Tuesday. She's been a Tuesday ever since.
a0.idle2: Half my pay goes to my mother. The other half goes to Joss, apparently.

a0.broken: I still know how to set a bone. That's something to believe in, it turns out.
a0.stage4: Four heads stirring. I should be glad. I keep waiting to be glad.
a0.default: Bring them to me before you go down. A clean dressing is worth a prayer, whoever you pray to.

lines.a0: Ah! The Keeper! Pim Ashgrove, maps, charts, the occasional rumour pinned to the wall. Mostly rumours, lately.
lines.a1: When somebody at the Low Lantern gives you a lead, I pin it to its Door. Look for the little scroll on the echo.
lines.a2: Mind, the Doors shift. What's there one night isn't there the next. A lead turns up in maybe one run in three. Keep going back and it will turn up, I promise. Always by the third.

lines.a0: You brought this up from the Drowned Star? Put it down. Gently. Thank you.
lines.a1: I expected a weapon. Something to bind a monster, crack a ward. It isn't.
lines.a2: It's a cradle. A rune of holding, written the way you'd write a lullaby. It was made to keep something still, very gently, for a very long time.
lines.a3: And it's warm. Things like this are only warm while they're working.| It's getting cooler.

lines.a0: Seventy-one. Seventy-two. Seventy-th— they've gone black. Why have they gone black?
lines.a1: In rings, Keeper. Like something wet sat on them. Only the coins from the Trust's accounts. The rest are fine.
lines.a2: And the Trust's ledger doesn't balance. Every season, more goes out than comes in. Out where? There's nowhere to send it but down.

lines.a0: You want something in the Chronicle. Everyone does, lately. Most of them want the word "triumph".
lines.a1: You lay it out: the manifest, the roster, the letter signed P., the mirror's broken line. "Break no—".
lines.a2: No, or now. A crack's width between them.| And you want me to write that the Keep has been wrong for three hundred years.
lines.a3: If I write it, the Guild will read it. They won't stop. But people will know someone said it.
lines.warn0: Then it's written. In my own hand, so nobody can say a clerk did it.
lines.warn1: I read it. Four heads are loose already and the fifth echo is falling in on itself. Do you want her to wake with no one at the door?| The Guild goes on. But I'll have the shelters dug.
lines.wait: Sure is a luxury, Keeper. Come back when you can't afford it.

a3: "Not yet. I need to be sure."

lines.a0: I've left every chapter as it was written. We believed it when we wrote it. That matters.
lines.a1: But I've added notes in the margins, in green ink, so you can see what we know now beside what we thought then.
lines.a2: Read them in order. It's the only way they make sense.| It's the only way any of it does.

lines.a0: Maren Holt. Guildmaster. I keep the roster, I post the bounties, and every morning I read the Wall of the Fallen out loud.

a1.fallen: There are names on it already, under your Keep. I read them every morning. Let's not add more. Bring them home.
a1.none: Nobody's on it yet, under your Keep. I'd like to keep it that way. Bring them home.

maren: The Aldane Trust posted another bounty. Four hundred gold for the thing in the Deep Forge. Generous people.
First Door broken! I've hung your names in the hall. Don't let it go to your heads.
The Trust doubled the bounty on the Third Door. Nobody's complaining. I'm not complaining.
Half the board's empty. Folk say the wells taste wrong. Wells don't fight back, I tell them.
Notice from the Guild council: "The disturbances are the Queen's death throes. Press on." I posted it. I read it twice first.
New recruits came in shaking. I don't blame them. I'm shaking, and I've seen worse. I think.
I read the Wall this morning, same as always. Then I read the names of the hands. Both lists, every morning, from now on.
ilvane: The Chronicle is open. Every echo you break, I write down. Try to make it worth the ink.
Chapter One. I wrote "triumph". It felt like a triumph.
Chapter Two. I wrote "triumph" again. I am going to have to find another word.
I wrote "triumph" three times in this chapter. I am going to have to stop writing "triumph".
The lanterns flare when an echo breaks. I've always written that they flare in celebration. I've started to wonder.
Every reading candle in the Chronicle went out. I am writing this by the light of a candle Bet lent me.
The last chapter is written. I left a blank page after it. Old habit. Someone always comes after.
pim: Five Doors, five echoes, one map. Well. Several maps. They disagree.
The First Door's map stopped moving. Maps aren't supposed to move in the first place, but they were. Now they don't.
The Second Door map has gone green at the edges. Mould, probably. Probably.
The Sixth Door is on the map where I drew it. It is also somewhere else on the map. I didn't draw that.
Frost on the ink. Inside. I have started wearing gloves to draw.
All the Doors are open on the map now. Even the Sixth. Especially the Sixth.
The maps are just maps again. I'm almost disappointed. Almost.
hulda: Forge burned too hot the night the First Door broke. Couldn't bank it. Never seen that.
Got a crate in stamped with five mouths. Fine work. I sent it back.
Trust paid in coin. Coin's been underwater. Tastes of ink. I took it anyway.
Frost on the blades this morning. In my forge. I don't like what that says about my forge.
I'm forging for the defence now. Whoever's defending. Buy something, it pays for the rest.
Back to horseshoes and hinges. Good. I missed hinges.
fennick: Potions, poultices, and advice. The advice is free and nobody takes it.
Every hearth in the Keep burned too hot, and every pot of honey crystallised. I am old, dear. I notice things.
All my herbs bloomed in one night and rotted by morning. I've sent for more. I've sent twice.
Somebody's buying all my willow bark "for Kiln Row". Kiln Row hasn't had any. I asked.
Ice in the tinctures. You could skate on my syrups.
I'm rationing. Not the rich, dear. Everyone else. Don't argue with an old woman.
I'll have a proper garden again by spring. Ordinary plants. Ordinary weeds. Lovely.
sabeline: Enchanting is just persuasion, applied to metal. Bring me something worth persuading.
The runes on my anvil flickered when the First Door broke. They've never flickered.
Wards are borrowed things, Keeper. Every ward borrows from something. I've started asking what.
Bring me anything you find with a rune of holding on it. Anything. I need to know how many there were.
The wards on the Keep gate failed at dawn. All of them at once, like a held breath let go.
Every ward we had was borrowed from her dreams. I'm writing new ones. From scratch. It's slow.
My new wards hold. They're ugly. They're mine.
kost: You want to live down there? Then you train up here. Simple.
Good clear on the First Door! Again! Faster this time!
Recruits are keen this season. The Trust's bounties do that. I don't trust keen.
Three of my recruits won't hold a sword. Says it's no good. Says something's listening.
Found the practice dummies frozen solid this morning. Hit them anyway. Builds character.
I'm drilling cooks and clerks to hold a line. They're terrible. They're trying. That's a line.
Grounds are open. Bring your reserves. Life's for living again.
pell: Everything in the Vault is counted. Twice. I count it twice.
Your gold's safe, Keeper. Nobody's touched it but me, and I only count it.
The Trust's deposits have doubled. I've had to buy a second ledger.
The Trust's coins went black in rings. Only the Trust's. I have counted them four times.
Tribute ledger doesn't match. More goes out than comes in, every season, for years. Out where?
Someone has been emptying us into the mountain for years. I counted it. I counted all of it.
Kiln Row's money is back in the Vault, labelled by family. I'm giving it back one name at a time.

heads.cinder: I was dreaming of a forge that never cooled. Warm. Endless. Mine. Who taught you to put out fires, little ones?
heads.rootbound: My garden is dead. Every grave I tended. Every flower. I will plant another, and you will be in it.
heads.drowned: I had a library of every word ever drowned. I was reading. You closed the book.
heads.mirror: I could see only myself, and I was beautiful. Now I see you. I see everything a mirror sees.
heads.starfall: You sang me five lullabies, little lantern-bearers. Then you came and put out every one. I am awake. I remember who did it.

eulogy.line: I read {name}'s name off the Wall this morning. {clears}, {kills} foes put down. {cause}We'll read it every morning.
